maps.title: Transcription + translation
maps.description: Expression end to end: what is transcribed together with what reaches the ribosome, so a gene regulated at translation separates from one regulated at transcription.

maps.title: Transcription + protein abundance
maps.description: Message against protein: genes whose transcript and protein levels agree sit apart from those where one is buffered against the other.

maps.title: Translation + protein abundance
maps.description: Ribosome occupancy against how much protein is actually there, which is where turnover and stability show up.

maps.title: Transcription + fitness
maps.description: When a gene is expressed against what losing it costs -- the classic pairing for finding stage-specific essential genes.

maps.title: Fitness + protein abundance
maps.description: Whether what a knockout costs tracks how much of the protein there is: abundant-and-dispensable and scarce-and-essential are both interesting neighbourhoods.

maps.title: Fitness + localization
maps.description: Where a protein is together with what losing it costs, the pairing that separates the essential machinery of one compartment from its dispensable passengers.

maps.title: Protein abundance + localization
maps.description: Abundance and compartment together: the axes a spatial proteomics experiment actually measures, without the transcriptional variation on top.

maps.title: Sequence + localization
maps.description: What a protein's sequence and fold say, beside where it goes -- the signal a targeting prediction lives on.

maps.title: Sequence + fitness
maps.description: Conservation, domains and disorder against what losing the gene costs: essentiality against how constrained the sequence is.

maps.title: Sequence + transcription
maps.description: Sequence and fold beside expression, so a conserved housekeeping gene separates from a variable, stage-restricted one.

maps.title: Regulation + transcription
maps.description: The regulatory layer -- chromatin, RNA stability, splicing -- with the transcription it produces, so a gene held down by its chromatin separates from one that is simply off.

maps.title: Regulation + PTM
maps.description: Two layers of control that are not the message itself: chromatin and RNA on one side, post-translational modification on the other.

maps.title: Relation + protein abundance
maps.description: Who a protein is found with, beside how much of it there is: the pairing a complex should show up on, since a complex's members are usually present in proportion.

maps.title: Relation + localization
maps.description: Interaction evidence with compartment, so a complex confined to one organelle separates from a promiscuous hub.

maps.title: PTM + protein abundance
maps.description: Modification against abundance: whether a heavily modified protein is a scarce regulator or an abundant substrate.

maps.title: Fitness + relation
maps.description: What losing a gene costs, beside who it works with -- the evidence a genetic-interaction argument is made from.

maps.title: Transcription + translation + protein abundance
maps.description: The whole expression cascade in one map -- transcript, ribosome, protein -- so a gene regulated at any one step separates from one regulated at all three.

maps.title: Transcription + translation + fitness
maps.description: Expression at both levels against cost, the fullest picture of when a gene is needed.

maps.title: Fitness + protein abundance + localization
maps.description: Cost, amount and place: the three questions a functional genomics screen is usually read for.

maps.title: Sequence + relation + localization
maps.description: What a protein is, who it is with and where it is -- structure-first evidence with no expression in it at all, so an expression label scored here cannot be reading itself back.

maps.title: Regulation + transcription + translation
maps.description: The whole message layer: how it is regulated, what is made and what is read.

maps.title: Sequence + transcription + fitness
maps.description: Conservation, expression and cost, the three axes a candidate gene is usually triaged on.

search.ranked_on: umap_gallery.structure: sqrt(search.map_quality score x mean silhouette of the clustered points, rescaled to 0..1). No label is read, so the search cannot tune a map onto what it is scored on.

scoring.bound: Wilson 95% lower bounds of precision and recall, combined as F1
